title: Small or large, every coin and valley is written.
subtitle: Uthman's camels and the ordinary traveler

row.title: by the best
sub: of what they used to do

then: When the Prophet ﷺ urged spending on the army of hardship for Tabuk, Uthman bin Affan pledged {reward}a hundred camels, then a hundred more, then a hundred more.{/reward} The verse also counts the {idea}small contribution{/idea}. Qatadah said: the farther people go from their families for Allah, the nearer they are to Him.
now: You are not Uthman. Your gift is ten dollars and a Saturday morning driving boxes to the food bank. {reward}Small or large, the verse says it is written.{/reward} And Allah repays by the best thing you did, not the average.
old: Only big sacrifices really count with Allah.
new: Every small or large effort is written, and repaid by my best.
try: Give something small today for a good cause and trust that it is recorded.

title: Not everyone goes out; some must stay and learn.
subtitle: A community that keeps its knowledge

picture.label: How the community divided its work

then: Ibn Abbas said the believers should not all leave the Prophet ﷺ alone. While some went out, others stayed {idea}and learned what was revealed{/idea}, then taught the returning group: Allah revealed this to your Prophet, and we learned it. The verse speaks of gaining {idea}understanding in the religion{/idea} and warning one's people.
now: In your family or circle, maybe no one has really studied the faith. Everyone is busy with work and kids, and questions go to random videos. {idea}The verse says someone needs to be the one who learns, then comes back and shares.{/idea} It could be you.
old: Learning the faith deeply is for scholars, not for people like me.
new: My circle needs someone who learns and brings it back.
try: Learn one thing about your faith properly today, and share it with one person.

title: Allah is with those who have taqwa.
subtitle: A battlefield command and how it ends
then: This command was given to the believers in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, as part of the Tabuk era. Ibn Kathir explains the firmness as {trap}in battle{/trap}, and says the complete believer is {reward}kind to his believing brother.{/reward} He reads the closing words as: trust in Allah, knowing {idea}He is with you if you fear and obey Him.{/idea}
now: Your life is not a battlefield. What carries over is how the verse ends: success rests on {idea}taqwa{/idea}, not on how tough you look. At home, at work, in the family chat, the believer is known first for softness with those close to them.
old: Being strong and tough is what wins.
new: Allah's company comes with taqwa, and that is what truly wins.
try: Be extra gentle today with one family member you are usually short with.

title: Which of you did this surah increase in faith?
subtitle: The same verses, two very different effects
then: Some hypocrites asked each other mockingly, after a surah came down, {trap}which of you has had his faith increased by it?{/trap} Allah answered that the believers {reward}did grow in faith, and rejoiced.{/reward} Ibn Kathir calls this one of the strongest proofs that faith increases and decreases.
now: You sit in a Friday khutbah. The person next to you scrolls. You hear one line that lands, and your chest feels lighter for the rest of the day. {reward}Same words, same room.{/reward} The verse says what you bring to the Quran shapes what it does to you.
old: My faith is just at whatever level it is.
new: Each verse I take in with an open heart can raise my faith.
try: Read a few verses today slowly, and ask Allah to increase your faith through them.

title: The same medicine makes a sick heart sicker.
subtitle: When guidance meets a diseased heart
then: Ibn Kathir says the surah only {trap}adds doubt and suspicion{/trap} to what those with sick hearts already had. He gives a picture: {trap}someone upset by a certain food{/trap} gets more upset when fed more of it. Yet the Quran is {reward}a healing{/reward} for those who believe.
now: Every reminder irritates you lately. The khutbah feels preachy, the friend's post feels judgmental, the verse feels aimed at you. {idea}Before blaming the reminder, check the heart that is receiving it.{/idea}
old: If a reminder annoys me, the reminder must be the problem.
new: If guidance irritates me, my heart may need healing.
try: Next time a reminder annoys you, pause and ask Allah to soften your heart toward it.

title: Tested once or twice a year, and still no turning.
subtitle: Missing the lesson in hardship
then: Mujahid said they were tested {trap}with drought and hunger.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that they neither repented from their past sins {trap}nor learned a lesson for the future.{/trap} The trials came again and again, and nothing changed.
now: Every winter the same scare: a lump, a layoff rumor, a car crash that almost happened. You promise to change, then the fear fades and the promise fades with it. {idea}The verse asks you to let the next trial actually change something.{/idea}
old: Hard times are just something to survive and forget.
new: Each trial is a chance to repent and remember before the next one.
try: Recall your last real scare. Do one thing today you promised to do back then.

title: Does anyone see you? Then they slipped away.
subtitle: Turning from the truth, and being turned
then: When a surah was revealed, the hypocrites would look right and left, {trap}does anyone see you?{/trap}, then slip away. Ibn Kathir says they do not stay where truth is being declared. He links it to another verse: {trap}when they turned away, Allah turned their hearts away.{/trap}
now: The talk at the masjid starts, and you glance at the door, check your phone, slip out during the pause. No one notices. {idea}The verse notices.{/idea} Each small exit makes the next one easier, until staying feels impossible.
old: Leaving early does not matter if no one sees.
new: Each time I turn from the truth, my heart turns a little further.
try: Stay until the end of the next reminder or talk you attend, even if you want to leave.

title: Your hardship weighs on him; he is eager for you.
subtitle: The Messenger's ﷺ care for his people
then: After a long surah of warnings, it closes with mercy. Ibn Kathir notes this verse is among {idea}the last revealed{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}I am holding you by the waist so you do not fall into the Fire, like moths.{/reward} He also said this religion is easy.
now: You may picture the faith as a list of things you get wrong. This verse shows a face full of concern for you. Every struggle you have, the debt, the anxiety, the habit you cannot break, {reward}would have grieved him ﷺ.{/reward} He wanted ease for you.
old: The Prophet ﷺ feels distant, a source of rules.
new: The Prophet ﷺ is grieved by my hardship and eager for my good.
try: Send salawat on the Prophet ﷺ ten times today, thinking of his care for you.

title: If they turn away, Allah is enough for me.
subtitle: The last words of the surah

row.title: their acceptance
sub: if they agree, I am okay

then: The surah ends with the Prophet ﷺ told what to say if people turn away from what he brought: {idea}Allah is sufficient for me.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the Throne is above all creation, and {reward}everything is under His power{/reward}. Zayd bin Thabit said he found this final verse with Khuzaymah bin Thabit.
now: You did your best: the gentle advice, the patience, the invitation. And they still walked away, unfollowed you, stopped calling. {idea}You do not have to carry that alone.{/idea} Hasbiyallah. The One who holds the Throne is enough.
old: If people reject me, I have failed and I am alone.
new: When people turn away, Allah is still enough for me.
try: When someone turns away from you today, say: Hasbiyallahu la ilaha illa Huwa, alayhi tawakkaltu.
